paper text.text: Retain a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of $B_1+bd+cw$. It uses $bd$, since deleting this edge leaves the planar graph $B_1+cw$. The vertices of this subdivision outside $\{b,c,d,w\}$ may lie in different components of $B_1-\{b,c,d,w\}$. By \eqref{r2:cross-connectivity}, every such component has a neighbor at $w$ and at $b$ or $d$. Retain a $b$--$d$ path in $D_1$ and a neighbor of $c$ outside $\{b,c,d,w\}$. Since $D_1$ avoids $c,w$, the internal vertices of the path lie in one component of $B_1-\{b,c,d,w\}$. The chosen neighbor of $c$ lies in one such component as well. Thus at most two further components are needed. By Lemma~\ref{r2:retained-components}, contract each to one vertex and keep a minimal set of attaching edges satisfying \eqref{r2:cross-connectivity}. The retained subdivision keeps $B+ac+bd$ nonplanar. In the other three tests, the bridge containing $D_1$ is still adjacent to all of $X$. The conditions in \eqref{r2:cross-connectivity} keep the interior of $B$ connected and give every attachment an interior neighbor. Thus the reduction is allowed and keeps all four tests nonplanar, so minimality leaves $B$ unchanged. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} lists every possible $B_1$, with attachments $b,c,d,w$, added edges $bd,cw$, the original edges $bw,dw$ permitted on the subdivision, the requirements \eqref{r2:cross-connectivity}, and at most two further interior components. Adding $a$ and the three pairs of twins gives the $5{,}819$ candidates in~\supp{E17}. Each has nonplanar $B$, a $K_5$ minor, a separating set of at most two vertices, or a proper nontoroidal minor.
